labelProposals.conflictsDescription: Folders and files the importer left in place. A folder pair means the name it wanted is taken by a folder holding a different release: compare the two and remove or rename one. A single file is not an archive or music, or is an archive nothing could extract: move it away, or replace it with a good copy. The importer warns about each one once, never touches it, and forgets it on the next cycle after it is gone or changed.
labelProposals.description: Releases the importer could not place. Confirming a proposal that carries a catalogue number teaches the rule, so every later release on that label goes through on its own.

mode.body: Everything in the library is either a song or a set: a recording of ten minutes or longer, such as a festival set or a podcast. Pick what you browse most; you can switch at any time at the top of the screen.

home.body: Home is made of sections. 'Button' puts a section as a tile at the top, 'Overview' gives it a row of tracks of its own, 'Off' hides it. Memories — today's releases from earlier years — have a switch of their own.

display.title: How should lists look?
display.body: The same track often exists several times in the library (a release, a compilation, a radio edit). Deduplication shows one. Lines per row decide how much you see per track, and the confirmation keeps one tap from downloading a three-hour set.

downloads.title: Download over mobile data?
downloads.body: Downloads stay on your phone, connection or not. Sets are big; with 'wifi only' on, a download waits until you are home.

tour.title: Tour
tour.body: The short tour of the settings that matter most, the same one your first visit opened.

home.title: Home
home.body:
Home is where you start: tiles at the top for the places you visit often, rows of tracks below. Which sections you see, and whether each is a tile or a row, is yours to set under Settings › General › Home.

On the website your presets (saved searches) sit on Home too; on the phone they have a tab of their own, Favorites.

mode.title: Songs and sets
mode.body:
The library holds two kinds of recording. A song is under ten minutes; anything longer is a set: a festival recording, a podcast, a mix. The Songs/Sets switch — in the sidebar on the left, at the top of the screen on the phone — decides what you see everywhere.

Some entries only exist in one mode. Labels and Lineups belong to songs; Festivals and Podcasts to sets. Artists, albums, genres and years are in both.

browse.title: Browse
browse.body:
The library can be browsed by artist, album, genre, label, podcast, festival, year, lineup and BPM (tempo). On the website those sit in the sidebar under Library; on the phone as tiles under Browse. The two lists are the same.

A genre or label page shows everything carrying that tag, with filters and sorting at the top. The sidebar also lists your favourite genres, or — until you have picked any — the biggest ones.

search.title: Search and presets
search.body:
The search box at the top searches titles, artists and albums. For more there is advanced search: every attribute (genre, label, year, rating, length, festival…) as a list, to combine.

Such a search can be saved as a preset. A preset is a dynamic playlist: it refills itself every time you open it, so new tracks that match are in it by themselves.

favorites.title: Favourites and ratings
favorites.body:
A heart on a track puts it among your favourites; the Favourites list (in the library) collects them. You can also give stars, one to five. Five means 'this is a favourite'; one means 'not my thing' and never 'get rid of it' — a rating never removes anything.

Ratings feed advanced search and the daily mixes, which bring highly rated tracks back more often.

feeds.title: Release Radar and daily mixes
feeds.body:
Release Radar shows what came out this week in the styles you play — the small shares of your taste included, so the list does not collapse into one genre.

The daily mixes are five selections a day: soft, mid and hard (by the genre's hardness), plus the artist and the label of the day. They lean on what you have never played and on what you rated highly. An empty feed means nothing matched, not that something broke.

memories.title: Memories
memories.body: Memories are releases with a birthday today: released on this day in an earlier year. One tile per year; open one and hear what came out then. They appear once the library has tracks with a full release date, and on Home when you switch that on.

stats.title: History and listening stats
stats.body:
History is the list of what you played, newest first. Listening stats add it up: how much, when in the day and the week, and your most played tracks, artists and labels over 30 days, 12 months or all time.

The page is honest about what it does not know: plays that match no track in the library count in the total but appear in no ranking.

queue.title: Playback and queue
queue.body:
Tapping a track plays it and puts the list around it in the queue. The queue (the button next to the player) shows what is coming; you can shuffle it, clear it or save it as a playlist.

On the phone a tap on the mini player opens the full Now Playing screen, with lyrics when there are any. The equalizer lives in the player menu and remembers your setting.

downloads.title: Downloads and offline
downloads.body:
Tracks and sets you download stay on your phone and play without a connection; you find them under Downloads. With 'wifi only' on, a download waits until there is wifi.

When the connection drops you see only what you downloaded. Searching and browsing the server pause until it is back.

car.title: Car mode
car.body: Car mode is a screen with big buttons for the road: play, next, previous, shuffle, and the microphone. It opens by itself when the phone connects to a car, or by hand from the profile menu.

voice.title: Voice
voice.body: The microphone (under Browse and in car mode) understands ordinary sentences: 'play hardstyle', 'sets from Defqon', 'something by Angerfist', 'next'. The screen shows what MuMa understood and lists everything you can say.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body:
General: language, Home sections, display and what is kept on your account. Advanced: password and which sort options you see. About: versions, what is new and the update check. Device (phone only): cache, bitrates, downloads, car and diagnostics.

Settings are kept on your account, so phone and website stay the same.

management.title: Management
management.body: As an administrator, Management (profile menu) holds the server side: scanning, the tagger and curation of artists, genres, labels and podcasts, the downloaders, radio and news, users and their requests, health and the log. This manual is about listening; Management explains itself page by page.

curation.notInLibrary: Not in the library yet — rules can already be recorded
curation.artistGone: This artist no longer exists in the library.
curation.artistMbidHelp: The MBID links this artist to MusicBrainz. Leaving it empty clears the link.
curation.mbidInvalid: That is not an MBID. Paste only the id, not the whole MusicBrainz URL.
curation.mbidInvalidShort: That is not an MBID. Paste only the id.
curation.aliasesHint: Other spellings this artist appears under, for example 'DJ Angerfist'.
curation.aliasSelf: An artist is not an alias of itself.
curation.retagQueued: {count} files are queued to be retagged.

markedSome.one: {base} 1 file is queued to be retagged.
markedSome.other: {base} {count} files are queued to be retagged.

curation.hardnessInvalid: Must be a whole number between 0 and 100, or empty.
curation.genreNotApproved: This genre has not been approved by curation
curation.parentsHint: Broader genres this genre belongs to. The tagger adds them to every track with this genre.
curation.parentNotAllowed: Not possible: a genre cannot roll up into itself or into one of its own subgenres, and appears only once.
curation.hardnessHelp: 0 (soft) to 100 (hard). Decides which of the soft, middle or hard daily mix this genre ends up in. Leaving it empty hands the genre back to the automatic estimate.
curation.subgenresHelp: Genres that roll up into this genre. Change them on their own page.
curation.genreNotEditableBefore: Curation decides whether a genre exists; this page edits a genre that has already been approved. This genre is on
curation.genreNotEditableAfter: , so there is nothing to set — the tagger writes it nowhere.
curation.reviewFirst: Review it first under Management → Genre curation.
curation.genreRulesHelp: Every track below gets these genres in the next tagger run.
curation.catalogHelp: Read from the release folder names; only the EPs folder counts. Only the observed range counts: nothing is claimed before the lowest or after the highest number, and a number that is not present may also have been skipped by the label.
curation.catalogEmpty: No readable catalogue numbers in this label's folders.
curation.filesOutsideRoot: {count} files of this label are outside the EPs folder and were not counted.
curation.absentTruncated: {count} numbers not present — too many to list; probably one folder name is far outside the series.
curation.allPresent: Everything within the observed range is present.
curation.parentLabelHelp: The label this sublabel belongs to. Not used by the tagger yet.
curation.parentPlaceholder: id of the parent label, empty to clear
curation.catidHint: A release with this number in its folder name is assigned to this label.

bpm.subtitle: Everything at one tempo. Pick a tempo, a bar or a range.
bpm.reliableHelp: Only tempos that were measured, or a tag the analysis agrees with inside the genre's tempo.
bpm.histogramHint: Tap a bar to pick that tempo.
bpm.pickPrompt: Pick a tempo or a range to see the tracks.
bpm.coarseNote: ≈ means roughly measured: the old analysis could only produce steps of about 4 to 9 BPM (152, 156, 161 ...). Precise measurements are on their way; until then the margin absorbs the rounding.
bpm.emptyReliable: No reliable tempos here. Switch off Reliable to see the rough values too.

source.folded: Doubled or halved into the genre's tempo
